subject.title: Telegram voice message delayed ~15 minutes before agent dispatch, then run aborts

question: What should Telegram do when a source message is already stale at dispatch time or a voice direct-message run aborts before any visible reply?
rationale: The code can measure latency and emit a fallback, but the restart threshold, user-visible failure text, and whether DM no-response remains silent are maintainer product decisions.

options.title: Define latency and fallback contract
options.body: Choose a source-message age threshold plus a visible aborted/no-reply DM behavior, then implement and prove it with Telegram tests and live proof.

options.title: Limit this to observability
options.body: Add source-message latency logging/watchdog evidence only and leave user-visible fallback changes to a separate delivery policy issue.

options.title: Consolidate into related issues
options.body: Close this only if maintainers decide #78079 and #91652 should jointly own the remaining delay and voice-reply-drop work.

recommendation.title: Define latency and fallback contract
recommendation.body: Choose a source-message age threshold plus a visible aborted/no-reply DM behavior, then implement and prove it with Telegram tests and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The first decision point is the Telegram polling/dispatch liveness contract that their recent getUpdates stall work owns most directly.
